              SAVE THE LAMPASAS’ APPEAL OF SOAH ORDER NO. 13
          REGARDING DENIAL OF HEARING REQUEST ON ROUTE ADEQUACY

                                     EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

    Given the permanence and widespread potential impacts of the results of this Appeal, this

Executive Summary is provided for the convenience of the Chairman, Commissioners and your

Staffs.

         The Order improperly cancels the Route Adequacy Hearing and reaches conclusions on
          route adequacy thereby foreclosing consideration of routing alternatives presented by
          Save the Lampasas.

         The Applicants’ consultants’ Routing Study states that they could find limited corridors to
          follow for routing alternatives in eastern Burnet County.

         Save the Lampasas experts have identified two specific existing corridors that should be
          considered for routing alternatives in this proceeding.

         Neither the Applicants Consolidated Response, or Order No. 13 refute (or even address)
          the potential viability of these alternatives.

         The Order prematurely reaches a conclusion on route adequacy without holding a hearing
          based on a wholesale adoption of conclusory statements made in the Applicants
          Consolidated Response. The facts underlying these assertions are disputed and can only
          be evaluated in a hearing.




                                                                                                         001
                                                                                      Page 2 of 13


   The impacts of this case on the Texas Hill Country would be far reaching and in
    perpetuity. The Commission should have a reasonable number of geographically diverse
    routing alternatives available to them at the end of this case for all portions of the study
    area.

   Commission precedent holds that limited routing alternatives that fail to comply with the
    applicable statutory and regulatory criteria can (and did in the Gillespie to Newton case)
    result in a Final Order denying the entire CCN application after a proposal for decision
    was entered. This precedent involved some of the very same proposed routing segments
    as are presented in this case in Burnet County.

   Given the timing and procedural complications of the decision to cancel the route
    adequacy hearing in Order No. 13, we respectfully request that the Commission grant this
    request and consider holding the hearing on route adequacy directly for administrative
    efficiency.

 SAVE THE LAMPASAS’ APPEAL OF SOAH ORDER NO. 13 REGARDING DENIAL
        OF HEARING REQUEST ON ROUTE ADEQUACY CHALLENGE

        This Appeal is filed regarding State Office of Administrative Hearing (SOAH) Order No.

13 Denying Motions for Route Adequacy Hearing and Cancelling Hearing on Route Adequacy.

As the name suggests, SOAH Order No. 13 denies the request for a hearing on route adequacy

filed by Save the Lampasas - an aligned group of intervenors consisting of over 50 noticed

landowners in Burnet County as well as more than 600 community members who support these

efforts.1 This appeal is necessary and materially affects the course of the proceeding because

without a route adequacy hearing, the ALJs and the Public Utility Commission of Texas’s

(Commission) available choices for routes to approve at the end of the case will be unduly

limited.2 The Commission should have a reasonable number of geographically diverse routes

that comply with the applicable routing criteria presented to them at the end of the case in order




        1
          See Save the Lampasas Updated Motion to Intervene (Apr. 27, 2026). Order No. 13 also denies separate
Route Adequacy Challenges and requests for hearing file by the Burnet County Commissioners Court, 4K Land and
Cattle Company, and Dub Z. Johnson.
        2
            Accordingly, this appeal is brought pursuant to 16 TAC § 22.123.




                                                                                                                 003
                                                                                               Page 4 of 13


to appropriately address the impacts of the proposed line on affected property owners,

communities, and the State of Texas.

        If SOAH Order No. 13 stands, the Commission’s only routing options available will all

traverse the northeastern portion of Burnet County. Further, if the Commission approves such a

route, the impact on the property, the property owners, and the affected community will be

irreversible and in perpetuity. The Commission and the affected community deserve better.

        Save the Lampasas requests that a hearing be held on the adequacy of the routing

alternatives available for consideration by the Administrative Law Judges (ALJs) and the

Commission in this proceeding.               More geographically diverse options that adhere to the

transmission line routing principles of paralleling available compatible corridors should be

available to the ALJs and the Commission in this case.


   I.          ORDER NO. 13 OMITS REFERENCE TO KEY ALTERNATIVE ROUTE
                                   PROPOSALS

        Order No. 13 states the legal standard for the burden of proof in a Route Adequacy

challenge as one where:

        . . . the parties challenging route adequacy “must present evidence showing the
        inadequacy of an application or routes and presenting other superior routes.” The
        applicants can then rebut this evidence by offering a reasoned justification as to
        why any proposed alternative routes should not be included. 3

However, the order is not consistent with this legal standard.                 Save the Lampasas’ Route

Adequacy Challenge and Request for Hearing includes two specific routing alternatives that

would follow compatible corridors in Burnet County. Order No. 13 makes no mention of these

routing alternatives put forward by Save the Lampasas. Order No. 13 relies heavily on the

Applicants’ Consolidated Response, which also offers no rebuttal to or “reasoned justification”

        3
            Order No. 13 at 6-7 (May 15, 2026) (internal citations omitted).




                                                                                                             004
                                                                                                     Page 5 of 13


as to why these routing alternatives specifically laid out in the Save the Lampasas filing and

attached exhibit maps were not included.                 In fact, the Applicants’ Consolidated Response

erroneously states that Save the Lampasas did not provide specific routes or exhibits of these

proposals and made no further mention of either option in their response. 4 The Route Adequacy

Challenge includes the following:5

          Attachment 2 – Map depicting Alternate Route G4 – following an existing transmission
                         line
          Attachment 3 – Map depicting Alternate Route G – following SH 183

Both of these routing alternatives follow existing corridors despite the “limited” corridors

identified by the Applicants’ consultants in this portion of Burnet County.

          For the reasons stated in the Save the Lampasas Route Adequacy Challenge, at minimum

a hearing should be conducted on the inclusion of these potentially superior routing options that

follow existing corridors (SH 183 and/or an existing transmission line) in a manner consistent

with the applicable statutory and regulatory criteria.             Neither the Applicants’ Consolidated

Response nor Order No. 13 provide a reasoned justification as to why it would be appropriate to

prevent the Commission from having these routing alternatives before them in this case, much

less why it would be appropriate to cancel a hearing on route adequacy to evaluate the facts

relevant to that determination.


    II.       ORDER NO. 13 PREMATURELY REACHES THE ADEQUACY OF ROUTES
                  BY FORECLOSING A HEARING ON DISPUTED FACTS

          The question before the Commission is limited to whether a hearing should be conducted

– not the merits of the route adequacy challenge itself. After evidence is presented at the

          4
              See, Applicants’ Consolidated Response at 8.
          5
           For the Commission’s convenience, these Attachments are included with this filing, and the entirety of
the Save the Lampasas Route Adequacy Challenge and Hearing Request is incorporated by reference.




                                                                                                                    005
                                                                                                           Page 6 of 13


hearing, the presiding officers can determine whether or not the Applicants should be directed to

evaluate the potential inclusion of these and other routes as alternatives in the Application. In

this instance the SOAH Order reaches a conclusion on the merits of route adequacy challenges

without affording the parties the opportunity to present their evidence. However, the basis on

which those conclusions on the merits are reached are based on disputed fact issues. For

example, Order No. 13 apparently mistakenly relies on assertions in the Applicants’

Consolidated Response in stating that “the routes are grouped into five corridors.” 6 This assertion

appears in the Applicants Consolidated Response as follows: 7




The record is unambiguous that there are only 3 routing “corridor options” in the Application in

eastern Burnet County which is the focus of Save the Lampasas’ Route Adequacy Challenge. 8




         6
             Order No. 13 at 9.
         7
             Applicants’ Consolidated Response at 18 with discussion to follow at pages 19-20.
          8
            See, excerpt from Applicants’ online map found here:
https://experience.arcgis.com/experience/d10c6b46ed714deb993e33448dd6096c; Also see, Save the Lampasas
Route Adequacy Challenge which makes clear that in this case not only are all routes limited to one of three routes in
Burnet County, but of the over 120 routes proposed in the Application approximately 70% of those routes utilize Link
G51.




                                                                                                                         006
                                                                                         Page 7 of 13


       Were the parties afforded the opportunity to present evidence at a hearing, these factual

disputes could be fully explored. Instead of giving the parties a chance to present all evidence,

the SOAH Order simply accepts the conclusory statements in the Applicants’ Consolidated

Response.

       Further, Order No. 13 refers to assertions made by Applicants with regard to the

feasibility of providing routing alternative to the north of Fort Hood. The Order refers to factual

assertions from the Applicants regarding cost and aviation impacts. The Applicants’ statements

constitute disputed facts that should be subject to a hearing. For example, the generalized

reference to aviation impacts does not ring true because the airstrip on Fort Hood is on the

southwest end of the Fort.9 Further the statements about diversions around the Fort to the north

being prohibitive are not consistent with the fact that the routes as proposed divert more than 17

miles to the south of the Fort.

       If given the opportunity for a hearing on route adequacy in this proceeding, Save the

Lampasas will provide evidence and testimony that is probative on these and other points raised

to support this route adequacy challenge. The witnesses who would be offered in support of this

route adequacy challenge will include Mr. Barry Smitherman, former chairman of the Public

Utility Commission of Texas and current professor at the University of Texas on electric utility

issues, and Mr. Aaron Brewer, who is an environmental and routing consultant and expert

witness with the firm of ESE Partners. Each of these witnesses can offer substantive information

that refutes the factual assertions of the Applicants on which Order No. 13 relies and that will

assist the Commission in evaluating this case.




       9
           Order No. 13 at 7.




                                                                                                       007
                                                                                                    Page 8 of 13


 III.        SUBSTANTIVE POINTS IN THE ROUTE ADEQUACY CHALLENGE ARE
                         DISMISSED WITHOUT MENTION

        In determining that the route adequacy process is to perform a “more cursory review” of

the application, the Order cites a case where a route adequacy hearing was held and where the

routes were determined to be inadequate because the applicant failed to include an alternate

substation site.10 That is one of the fact based determinations raised on the route adequacy

challenges here and one that should be explored in the route adequacy hearing.

        Order No. 13 also fails to address the fact that the Applicants have failed to provide a

reasoned justification for limitation of routing to this relatively narrow portion of the study area.

In fact, the evidence shows that the Applicants did not even consider any other routes. In

response to discovery the Applicants have answered:

                 b. No links in Coryell, Llano, Milam, or Mills counties were studied or
                 considered. Applicants have no responsive materials.

                 c. As explained in the Application and in response to subpart (a) above, no
                 proposed transmission facilities are located in Coryell, Llano, Milam, or Mills
                 counties.11

        The failure to include these routes is not consistent with the fact that the Applicants chose

to modify the style in this case to include counties to the North and South of the original study

area – i.e., Coryell, Milam, and Mills County. The Applicants’ consultants who present the

Environmental Assessment and Alternative Route Analysis were understandably limited in their

ability to explore all options. This case alone involves a very long, never-before constructed in

Texas 765-kV transmission line.                Further, these same consultants were essentially

Utilities, L.P. to Amend their Certificates of Convenience and Necessity for the North Edinburg to Loma Alta
Double-Circuit 345-Kv Transmission Line in Hidalgo and Cameron Counties, Docket No. 41606, SOAH Order No.
6 (Oct. 21, 2013).

(emphasis added).

                                                                                                       Page 9 of 13


simultaneously responsible for presenting the Environmental Assessment and Alternate Route

Analysis for multiple 765-kV projects and other 345-kV transmission line projects that were also

filed this year.12        It is important that the private property landowners and the affected

communities that are at the tail end of these cases be given full and fair consideration of all

routing alternatives.


   IV. COMMISSION PRECEDENT SUPPORTS THE NEED FOR HEARING TO
  DETERMINE ROUTE ADEQUACY GIVEN THIS PARTICULAR HILL COUNTRY
                         STUDY AREA

        The route adequacy challenge mechanism is included in these proceedings for the very

purpose of ensuring that the ALJs and the Commission are not faced with such limited options at

the end of the case as to necessitate denial of the Application.13 This was exactly the case in PUC

Docket No. 37448; Application of LCRA Transmission Services Corporation to Amend its

Certificate of Convenience and Necessity for the Gillespie to Newton 345-kV CREZ

Transmission Line in Gillespie, Llano, San Saba, Burnet, And Lampasas Counties, Texas (herein,

“Gillespie to Newton”). In that transmission line case, the Commission was so unfavorably

disposed as to the limited options available to them at the end of the case, they denied the

application, stating:

               However, based upon a weighing of the factors set out in PURA §37.056
        and P.U.C. SUBST. R. 25.101, the Commission determines that no route
        proposed in the application meets the requisite statutory and regulatory
        requirements. Consequently, the Commission denies the application. 14



        12
             See Attachment 1 for a list of at least some of these projects.
        13
             Much of this precedent was discussed in the Save the Lampasas Route Adequacy Challenge, but because
it received no mention in the Applicants’ Consolidated Response or Order No. 13, for the Commission’s benefit it is
also included here.
        14
            Application of LCRA Transmission Services Corporation to Amend its Certificate of Convenience and
Necessity for the Gillespie to Newton 345-kV CREZ Transmission line in Gillespie, Llano, San Saba, Burnet, and
Lampasas Counties, Texas, Docket No. 37448, Order at 1-2 (Apr. 28, 2010).




                                                                                                                      009
                                                                                       Page 10 of 13


       The proposed Gillespie to Newton proceeding involved some of the same geographic

areas of eastern Burnet County that are at issue in this proceeding. The Newton substation is near

the city of Lampasas, on the southeast side of Lampasas. Here is the routing alternative map for

the portion of the originally proposed Gillespie to Newton line: 15




       15
            Id. at Application at bates 156 (Oct. 28, 2009).




                                                                                                      010
                                                                                                          Page 11 of 13


         Below are the links proposed for this same area in the instant case:




         Several of the landowners participating on an aligned basis in Save the Lampasas, were

landowners who were affected by routes originally proposed in the Gillespie to Newton case. In

order to avoid a similar deficiency in routes presented to the Commission in this proceeding, the

Commission should, at minimum, allow for a hearing to explore the factual disputes surrounding

the route adequacy questions to ensure that ample and reasoned alternatives exist to create a

reasonable routing choice for the Commission.


                                               V.     CONCLUSION

         Oncor and LCRA bear the burden of proof to establish the Application presents an adequate

number of reasonably differentiated routes for each portion of the study area. The Commission

instituted the initial review of application adequacy to “ensure that the routes proposed in an application

are the result of a reasoned process that considered engineering principles, statutory and regulatory

factors, and Commission policy.”16 As stated in the Preliminary Order, consideration should be


         16
            Application of Wood County Electric Cooperative, Inc. for a Certificate of Convenience and Necessity for a
Proposed Transmission Line in Wood County, Texas, Docket No. 32070, Order on Appeal of Order No. 8 at 6 (Oct. 31, 2006).




                                                                                                                           011
                                                                                                         Page 12 of 13


given to the number of proposed alternatives, the locations of the proposed transmission line, and

any associated proposed transmission facilities that influence the location of the line. While the

Application presents numerous link combinations that can result in literally over 1000 routes, on

closer review, as it impacts Burnet County, there are only 3 routing alternatives, none of which

follow any compatible routing corridor, even though such corridors are available.                            This is

insufficient. The alternate routing corridors identified by Save the Lampasas that parallel an

existing roadway and transmission line are not only supported by the Commission’s substantive

rule, but such measures have also been encouraged by the author of S.B. 5066 and other House

Committee Chairs.17 Further, the consideration for an alternate substation location is also

appropriate for consideration in a route adequacy challenge.18 Evidence presented by Save the

Lampasas will support a study of routes north of Fort Hood that can be even further enhanced with

movement of the proposed new substation associated with this project to the north.

         Save the Lampasas respectfully requests that the Commission reverse Order No. 13 and

reinstate the hearing on route adequacy in this case. It is important to advise the Commission of

the procedural timing at issue here. The hearing on the merits in this case is currently scheduled

for June 8-12, 2026. It would procedural complications to have route adequacy determined after

the conclusion of that hearing. Further, given the importance of this portion of the case to the

Texas Hill Country and all potentially affected landowners and communities, for procedural and

administrative efficiency, Save the Lampasas respectfully requests that the Commission grant

this appeal and consider conducting this route adequacy hearing directly.
          17

         Oncor and LCRA bear the burden of proof to establish the Application presents an adequate

number of reasonably differentiated routes for each portion of the study area. The Commission

instituted the initial review of application adequacy to "ensure that the routes proposed in an application

are the result of a reasoned process that considered engineering principles, statutory and regulatory

factors, and Commission policy."16 As stated in the Preliminary Order, consideration should be

the conclusion of that hearing. Further, given the importance of this portion of the case to the

Texas Hill Country and all potentially affected landowners and communities, for procedural and

administrative efficiency, Save the Lampasas respectfully requests that the Commission grant

this appeal and consider conducting this route adequacy hearing directly.
